statement.description: One normalized, self-contained assertion with its qualifiers intact.

evidence_status.description: reported: authors state it as their result. quoted: verbatim from the paper. calculated: derived arithmetically from reported numbers (show the arithmetic in derivation). inferred: the analysing model's reading.

derivation.description: Required when evidence_status is calculated or inferred.

subject.description: Population, organism, task, corpus or system the claim is about.

magnitude.description: Verbatim value with units, e.g. '3.2x fewer false positives', 'F1 0.87 vs 0.81'.

conditions.description: Scope conditions under which the claim holds (coverage, platform, dataset, hyperparameters...).

qualifiers.description: Hedges and caveats preserved verbatim in spirit: 'may', 'in our setting', 'not statistically significant'.

support.description: At least one source locator. A claim without support is invalid.

section_origin.description: Which section the claim came from - used to separate primary results from introduction/related-work assertions.

is_primary_evidence.description: false when the claim only appears in introduction/related work, i.e. it is this paper reporting someone else's finding.

cited_source.description: When is_primary_evidence is false: whose work the claim belongs to, as printed.

confidence.description: Extraction confidence: how sure the analysing model is that the paper says this.

duplicate_of.description: Set by `kb validate` / human override when this claim restates another.
